name: logo-transparent-ground
story: A designer drew a sponsor lockup where the logo image has transparent holes in it and sits on a dark coloured backplate rect, so the plate colour shows through the logo's own gaps - a common real-world sponsor treatment - and exported the frame from Figma as SVG with ids on and text live.
idioms: no <?xml?> prolog, zero indentation, fill="none" on the root - Figma's standard SVG envelope
outer <g clip-path="url(#clip0_72_301)"> wrapping all art, with the matching <clipPath><rect width="1920" height="1080"/></clipPath> inside <defs>
the logo shape is a <rect fill="url(#pattern0_72_301)"> - Figma never writes a placed image as a positioned <image>
<pattern patternContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" width="1" height="1"> holding <use xlink:href="#image0_72_301" transform="scale(0.5)"> - scale(0.5) maps the 2px source into objectBoundingBox units
the <image> carrying the base64 data: URI is parked LAST inside <defs>, with only width, height and xlink:href
the ALPHA payload (two of four pixels fully transparent) used here because the logo has holes - different from the opaque payload used in the other two fixtures
xml:space="preserve" plus style="white-space: pre" on the text element, uppercase hex colours throughout
whyThisMatters: A logo with transparent pixels sitting on a coloured backplate is the standard sponsor treatment, and the alpha channel is what makes the plate colour visible through the logo's holes. If the importer flattens the alpha or substitutes an opaque background when it extracts the picture field, the sponsor's logo will bleed its own background colour over the plate instead of letting it show through - a visible on-air error. This file catches that failure because the ALPHA payload is the only image in the corpus where transparency is the content. It also states the whole ladder on a plate that carries text, which is what SVG_AUTHORING.md section 4 promises a growable panel is offered - wider first, then wrapping - rather than widening alone.
